(p-479) Surah "al-Jumu'ah" (The Congregation)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Glorification (tasbih) may be of three kinds. It may be glorification of creation (tasbih khilqah), meaning that when you look at anything, its very creation points you to the oneness of Allah (exalted is He) and to His being exempt from likeness to created things. Or it may be glorification of knowledge (tasbih ma'rifah), meaning that Allah, by His subtle kindness, places in everything that by which Allah (exalted is He) is known and declared pure. Do you not see His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra: 44]? Or it may be glorification of necessity (tasbih darurah), meaning that Allah causes every substance to glorify Him without it having any knowledge of this.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verse 2:

﴿He it is who raised up⦌, sent,

﴿among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves﴾, that is: He raised up a man who was unlettered among an unlettered people. It is also said: "from among themselves," like His saying: ﴿from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128], so that they know his lineage and his circumstances. And "al-ummi" (the unlettered) is derived from "ummat al-'Arab" (the nation of the Arabs), because they did not write or read, among the nations. It is also said: writing first began in al-Ta'if, and they took it from the people of al-Hira, and the people of al-Hira from the people of al-Anbar.

﴿recites to them His verses﴾, the Qur'an,

﴿and purifies them﴾, cleansing them from polytheism and the evil practices of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance),

﴿and teaches them the Book﴾, the Qur'an, (p-480) ﴿and the wisdom﴾, the Sunnah, or the understanding of the religion (fiqh),

﴿and indeed they were before, certainly, in manifest error﴾, disbelief and ignorance. Here "in" is a lightened form of the heavy "inna," and the lam is the indicator of it, meaning: they were in error, and you would not see an error greater than it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verse 3:

﴿Wa-ākharīna minhum﴾: it is in the genitive case (majrūr), coordinated (ma'ṭūf) upon "al-ummiyyīn" (the unlettered ones). The meaning is that He sent him (ﷺ) to the unlettered ones who were in his time, and to others of the unlettered ones.

﴿Lammā yalḥaqū bihim﴾: that is, they have not yet joined them, but they will join them. These are those who come after the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), or they are those who will come after them until the Day of Judgment. It has also been said: they are the non-Arabs (al-ʿajam). Alternatively, it is in the accusative case (manṣūb), coordinated upon the accusative in "wa-yuʿallimuhum" (and teaches them), meaning: he teaches them and teaches others, because the teaching, when it continues until the end of time, is all traced back to its first source, so it is as if he himself was the one who undertook everything that came about from it.

﴿Wa-huwa al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm﴾: in His empowering a man who was unlettered to undertake that great matter, and in His supporting him in it, and in His choosing him from among all of mankind.

﴿That﴾: the bounty God gave Muhammad, namely that he is a prophet to the people of his own age and a prophet to the people of later ages and to those who remain. It is ﴿That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whom He wills﴾, His giving it, and His wisdom requires it.

﴿And God is the possessor of great bounty﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 62, verse 5:

﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah﴾ means: they were charged with knowing it and acting by what is in it,

﴿then they did not carry it﴾, meaning they did not act (p-٤٨١) by it, so it is as though they did not carry it,

﴿are like a donkey carrying books﴾. *Asfar* is the plural of *sifr*, which is a large book. *Yahmilu* (﴿carrying﴾) is in the accusative position as a *hal* (circumstantial accusative), or in the genitive position as a *wasf* (descriptive qualifier), because the donkey is like the base man in the line of verse:

Indeed I pass by the base man who abuses me...........................

[The verse compares] the Jews, in that they are bearers of the Torah, its reciters, and its memorisers, yet they did not act by it and did not benefit from its signs, and in it is the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the good tidings of him, but they did not believe in him, to a donkey that carries large books of knowledge. It walks with them and understands nothing of them except what passes by its side and its back, namely the toil and fatigue. Everyone who has knowledge but does not act by his knowledge, this is his likeness.

﴿Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: evil as a likeness is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah, or: evil is the likeness of the people who deny, being like them, and they are the Jews who denied the signs of Allah that point to the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: at the time of their choosing wrongdoing, or: He does not guide those whom He knew in advance would be wrongdoers.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verse 6:

﴿Say, "O you who have Judaized (hada)﴾. "Hada, yahudu" means when one becomes a Jew (tahawwada),

﴿if you claim that you are allies of Allah, to the exclusion of the rest of mankind, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾. They used to say: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved." That is: if your statement is true, and you are certain of it, then wish upon Allah that He cause you to die and quickly transfer you to the abode of His honor which He has prepared for His allies. Then he said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verse 7:

﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forward.﴾ That is: because of what they committed of disbelief. There is no difference between *lā* (not) and *lan* (never); each of them negates the future. However, in *lan* there is emphasis and intensification that is not in *lā*. So He used the emphatic wording once, "and they will never wish for it" (*wa lan yatamannawhu*), and once without its wording: "and they will never wish for it" (*wa lā yatamannawnahu*).

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ This is a warning to them.

Say: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do," meaning, He will requite you with the punishment you deserve.

Commentary on the phrase "and you do not dare to wish for it, for fear that you will be seized by the consequence of your disbelief": you do not dare to wish for death, lest you be seized by the consequence of your disbelief.

"Then indeed it will meet you": this is certain, without doubt. The sentence is the predicate of "inna" (indeed). The "fa" (fa'/so) entered because "alladhi" (the one which) contains the meaning of a condition (shart), so it is treated as a conditional subject.

"Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do": He will then recompense you with the punishment that you deserve.

(p-482) ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday﴾. "Al-nida'" (the call): this is the adhan (the call to prayer). "Min" (from) is an explanation of and elaboration on "idha" (when). The day of Friday is the master of days. In a hadith: "Whoever dies on the day of Friday, Allah will record for him the reward of a martyr, and he will be protected from the trial of the grave."

﴿Fas'aw﴾: "famdu" (proceed). It has also been read as "fam-du" with this meaning. Al-Farra' said: "al-sa'y" (striving), "al-mudi" (going), and "al-dhahab" (going) are one and the same, and what is meant by it is not haste in walking.

﴿To the remembrance of Allah﴾, i.e., to the khutbah (sermon), according to the majority of scholars. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, used this as evidence that if the preacher limits himself to "al-hamdu lillah" (all praise is for Allah), it is permissible.

﴿And leave off trading﴾: he intended the command to abandon whatever distracts from the remembrance of Allah among the worldly preoccupations. He specifically singled out trading from among them because on the day of Friday buying and selling becomes abundant at midday (al-zawal). So it was said to them: hasten to the trade of the Hereafter, leave the trade of this world, and strive toward the remembrance of Allah, than which nothing is more beneficial or more profitable; and leave the trade whose benefit is slight.

﴿That﴾, i.e., striving toward the remembrance of Allah,

﴿is better for you﴾ than buying and selling,

﴿if you only knew﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verse 10:

﴿Then when the prayer is concluded﴾, i.e., performed,

﴿disperse in the land﴾, an imperative of permission (amr ibaha),

﴿and seek of Allah's bounty﴾: sustenance (al-rizq), or the seeking of knowledge (talab al-'ilm), or visiting the sick (iyadat al-marid), or visiting a brother for the sake of Allah (ziyarat akh fi Allah),

﴿and remember Allah much﴾, and give thanks to Him for having enabled you to perform His obligation,

﴿that you may prosper﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 62, verse 11:

﴿And when they see a trade or amusement, they scatter to it﴾: they dispersed away from you toward it. Its full sense is: "And when they see a trade, they scatter to it, or an amusement, they scatter to it." So one of the two was omitted, because the mentioned one indicates it. He specified trade because it was more important to them. It is related that "the people of Madinah were struck by hunger and high prices, so Dihyah ibn Khalifah arrived with a trade of olive oil from Syria (p-483) while the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the Friday sermon. They rose and went out to him, and only eight or twelve remained with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, had they all gone out, Allah would have kindled a fire upon them.'" And whenever a caravan came, they would welcome it with drums and clapping, and this is what is meant by "amusement."

﴿And they leave you﴾: on the pulpit,

﴿standing﴾: delivering the sermon. In this is evidence that the preacher should deliver the sermon standing.

﴿Say: what is with Allah﴾: of reward,

﴿is better than amusement and than trade, and Allah is the best of providers﴾: that is, the provision of Allah is not lost to them by leaving off the sale, for He is the best of providers.
